newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO'S COPAMEX TO LAUNCH IPO NEXT YEAR.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO'S COPAMEX TO LAUNCH IPO NEXT YEAR.

text.p: Mexican paper company Copamex SA will launch a global initial public offering next year worth between eight and 12 percent of its total capital, officials said on Tuesday.

"We plan to go public next year. For more than a year, we have been registered with the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV), so that should make the process easier," Alejandro Ferrigno, director of Copamex, told Reuters in an interview.
The head of Mexico's second biggest paper company said his company's sales would increase by 16 percent this year due to buying some assets from U.S. paper giant Kimberly-Clark's Mexican subsidiary.
Kimberly-Clark de Mexico was forced to sell the assets under Mexican anti-trust law after merging with Scott Paper's Mexican subsidiary.
"The goal in going public would be to institutionalize our company, amortize a big part of our debt and have greater cash flow to expand our respective businesses," Ferrigno said.
The Monterrey-based company, which began in 1928, produces about 500,000 tonnes per year of paper and expects to have annual sales of $500 million this year.
